what: A non-scrolling screen stage. Each scene has a length (in seconds) and flows on its own when left alone, looping back to the start at the end. Wheel, vertical drag and arrow keys wind or rewind by that amount: wheel delta accumulates into a target, the current value chases it by .2 per frame, and the target decays toward 0 by .2 so it stops with inertia. The current scene gets is-in (blur 8px resolving over .9s) and --fx-p (scene progress), and every frame fires fx:time (scene, progress, time, speed). Video, lines and copy are bound to it.

options.rate: Auto-flow speed (multiplier), default 1 — 0 means manual only
options.speed: Seconds wound per wheel 1, default .0016 (one notch 100 → about .8s)
options.follow: Share of the current value that follows the target (one 60fps frame), default .2
options.decay: Share by which the goal shrinks to 0, default .2
options.loop: If false, it stops at the end
options.[data-fx-part=scene]: Scene (child) · length in seconds in data-dur
options.[data-fx-part=knob]: (If present) bar handle that moves down following the total progress — --fx-total (0 to 1)
options.fx:time: Each Frame per element { index, progress, time, velocity }

from.where: index.js time engine — runs the first 10s · product loop 10s · usage scenes 6.08s ×4 · blue 7s · last 7s on their own and rewinds with the wheel (original wheel handling: _wheelDelta += .2 × (dist − wd), dist = lerp(dist, 0, .2))

note: When the stage covers the whole screen, the wheel is blocked (preventDefault) so the page does not scroll — only when the whole hero is used as the stage like the original. Text inside the scene is switched on and off in finer steps by the user with --fx-p or fx:time
